title: Invocation provenance, naming fallbacks, and telemetry for tool/function interop
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Customers are using both legacy function-style payloads and OpenAI-style tool descriptors. When callers specify tools/functions with overlapping or colliding names, or when model-side tool invocation formats differ (e.g., function signature vs tool metadata), we need a predictable, auditable way to select the right target and fall back gracefully without surprising downstream services. Additionally, developers want end-to-end invocation provenance and lightweight telemetry to diagnose misrouted calls and measure fallback rates.

Goals:
- Define an invocation selection algorithm that prefers exact matches but supports stable fallbacks (namespace-aware, prefix/alias resolution).
- Record invocation provenance metadata for each request (original payload form, resolved target, resolution path, fallback reason if any).
- Emit structured telemetry metrics and traces for: resolution latency, fallback frequency, ambiguous-name incidents, and misinvoke errors.
- Provide a migration path so teams can adopt the new name mapping without breaking existing clients.

Design (high level):
1) Name resolution precedence: 1) explicit runtime mapping in request (tool_id/tool_token) -> 2) exact name match across registries (tools then functions) -> 3) canonical alias map (user-provided + platform canonicalization) -> 4) best-effort semantic match using normalized tokens (lowercase, hyphen/underscore collapse).
2) Namespaces and scoping: support fully qualified names (project:service.function) and per-customer registries for private deployments. Default to hosted registry when no namespace is provided.
3) Invocation provenance payload: add a response header and runtime event containing {original_form, resolved_name, resolved_type, resolution_steps, fallback_reason, chosen_endpoint, cache_hit}. Stored as JSON in the audit log and surfaced in Console for 30 days.
4) Telemetry schema: counters and histograms exported to our metrics backend and OTLP traces with attributes: resolution.time_ms, resolution.path (string), fallback=true/false, collision=true/false, invoker.client_version.
5) Fallback policy: failures in preferred target trigger a soft-fallback to compatible target variants (e.g., function -> tool wrapper, or tool -> legacy function adapter) if compatibility metadata flags allowed. Each fallback increments the fallback counter and attaches fallback_reason in provenance.
6) Backcompat adapter: runtime will offer a lightweight adapter layer that translates OpenAI-style tool calls to legacy function RPC (and vice versa) when signatures match or when a mapping exists in the alias registry. This adapter will be opt-in per customer during rollout.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict matching minimizes accidental misinvocations but increases breakage during name churn. We choose stable fallback order + telemetry to allow visibility before tightening rules.
- Recording detailed provenance increases audit log size; retention defaults to 30 days but can be extended as an enterprise add-on.
- Automatic semantic matching can be surprising for ambiguous names; we will gate semantic matching behind a feature flag and require opt-in for private deployments.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (alpha, runtime-1.20): server-side name normalization + provenance header for internal beta customers. Telemetry counters emitted but semantic matching off.
- Phase 2 (beta): enable alias registry, allow customer-provided mappings, enable backcompat adapter as opt-in. Surface provenance in Console and add queryable dashboard for fallback rates.
- Phase 3 (GA): enable adapter for hosted customers with low-risk heuristics, promote feature flags to defaults for new customers, deprecate ambiguous legacy routes over 6 months with notifications.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for resolution precedence permutations and alias collisions.
- Fuzz tests with randomized name variants to measure false-positive matches.
- E2E tests exercising adapter translation for 5 canonical function->tool and tool->function cases across GPU and CPU backends.
- Load tests to ensure provenance recording adds <1% latency at P95.

Success metrics:
- Fallback rate <= 0.5% for new requests within 3 months of GA.
- Resolution latency P95 increase < 10ms relative to current baseline.
- Number of ambiguous-name incidents logged per customer < 2/week after initial migration guidance.

Implementation notes:
- New component: name-resolver service (stateless) with cache of alias maps and recent resolution results. Cache TTL default 60s; configurable per deployment.
- Audit events written to existing audit-log pipeline; lightweight provenance schema to avoid large payloads.
- Console: add a per-request resolution detail panel and an aggregated fallback dashboard.

Open questions:
- Should semantic matching be allowed for hosted customers by default, or always opt-in? (proposal: opt-in for hosted until we collect >30 days of telemetry).
- How to represent partial signature compatibility in provenance in a compact way?
- What escalation path for customer requests to enforce a specific mapping globally?

Migration guidance for customers:
- Provide a bulk alias import CSV and a UI to preview resolution results.
- Send deprecation notices for ambiguous names and recommended canonical names.
- Offer a migration window and an account-level toggle to enforce strict matching during cutover.
